sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Saluva Usurpation**: Saluva Narasimha, a powerful chieftain (Mahamandaleshwara) of Chandragiri, seized power in 1485, marking the first 'usurpation' in Vijayanagara history.
• **Military Consolidation**: The dynasty focused on strengthening the **Nayankara system**, delegating military and administrative authority to local governors to counter external threats.
• **Geopolitical Strategy**: The Saluvas faced a 'two-front war' against the **Bahmani Sultanate** in the north and the **Gajapatis of Odisha** in the east.
• **Key Metric**: The reign was short (20 years) but acted as a critical bridge between the Sangama and Tuluva dynasties, preventing the total collapse of the empire.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Founder; ruled from Chandragiri; focused on military expansion.
Military prowess and control over coastal trade ports.
Successor; ruled under the regency of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
Weak central authority; rise of the Tuluva power base.
Prelims: Transition point to Tuluva dynasty.

items.definition: A feudal-military system where the king granted land (Amaram) to Nayakas in exchange for military service and revenue. The Saluvas expanded this to ensure loyalty.
A high-ranking provincial governor or chieftain. Saluva Narasimha held this title before becoming Emperor, highlighting the shift from central to regional power.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Fortification**: Massive investment in the defense of Chandragiri and Penukonda.
• **Trade Diplomacy**: Encouraged horse trade from the Middle East via coastal ports to modernize the cavalry.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Internal rebellion by provincial governors and constant pressure from the Gajapatis of Odisha.
• **Solutions**: The rise of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka as a 'kingmaker' eventually stabilized the empire.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-S-T-A' (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu).
• **Decoded Meaning**: The chronological order of the four dynasties of the Vijayanagara Empire.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Saluva dynasty with the Tuluva dynasty. Remember: Saluva Narasimha founded the Saluva dynasty, but Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was the power behind the throne during the end of the Saluva period.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Realignment' to describe the Saluva period, emphasizing how military chieftains became the primary stakeholders in statecraft.

keyTakeaways: The Saluva dynasty represents the transition from hereditary rule to military-backed governance.
The Nayankara system was the backbone of Saluva administrative and military stability.
The dynasty served as a vital buffer, preventing the disintegration of the empire before the Tuluva golden age.
